proposed_comments.title: Limit menu-character suppression to shelf shortcuts
proposed_comments.body:
### Limit menu-character suppression to shelf shortcuts

**Severity:** `medium`

The current WM_MENUCHAR handler suppresses every unmatched menu character while Command Palette is open. That removes the system chime for the new shelf shortcuts, but it also swallows unrelated window mnemonics instead of preserving the normal default behavior. Please scope this handler to the shelf's Alt+0 through Alt+9 access keys so other menu characters continue through the usual path.

confidence.rationale: The fork fix changed the WM_MENUCHAR case to match only digit access keys, directly preserving non-shelf mnemonics while keeping the intended chime suppression.

proposed_comments.title: Refresh shelf shortcut bindings when visible items change
proposed_comments.body:
### Refresh shelf shortcut bindings when visible items change

**Severity:** `medium`

The shelf buttons and tooltip text bind ShortcutDigit with Mode=OneTime, so recycled or updated ItemsRepeater elements can keep stale Alt-key labels after the visible shelf items change. Users may see or invoke the wrong shortcut hint after pinning, unpinning, resizing, or overflow changes. Bind the shortcut digit and tooltip visibility one-way so the UI tracks the current QuickAccessShelfItem.

confidence.rationale: The current XAML uses OneTime on all ShortcutDigit consumers, and the fork fix updates those exact bindings to OneWay.

proposed_comments.title: Hide decorative overflow icons from UI Automation
proposed_comments.body:
### Hide decorative overflow icons from UI Automation

**Severity:** `medium`

The overflow flyout constructs IconBox instances in code and leaves them in the default accessibility view. Because each MenuFlyoutItem.Text already supplies the accessible name, the icon can become a separate unlabeled UI Automation node next to every overflow command. Set the generated icon's accessibility view to Raw, with the required automation namespace imports, to match the inline shelf icon behavior.

confidence.rationale: The inline shelf icon already sets AccessibilityView=Raw; the fork review added the same property to programmatically created overflow icons.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve Alt+Down for the focused filter dropdown
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve Alt+Down for the focused filter dropdown

**Severity:** `high`

The shell-level Alt+Down handler now expands the collapsed compact palette before the focused filter dropdown can process its normal open shortcut. When keyboard focus is inside FiltersDropDown, users pressing Alt+Down expect the filter menu to open, but the page intercepts the chord first. Detect that focused path and fall through to the default handling before attempting compact-palette expansion.

confidence.rationale: The fork fix added a VisualTreeHelper ancestor check for FiltersDropDown before the compact expansion path, directly preserving the existing dropdown shortcut.

proposed_comments.title: Localize the custom shelf landmark type
proposed_comments.body:
### Localize the custom shelf landmark type

**Severity:** `medium`

QuickAccessShelfSurface declares AutomationProperties.LandmarkType=Custom but only provides a generic name. For a custom landmark, screen readers need a localized landmark type to announce what region the user entered, especially because the shelf sits between search and results. Add the localized landmark resource for the quick access shelf alongside the existing automation name.

confidence.rationale: The current XAML marks the shelf as a custom landmark and the fork-only resource adds the missing LocalizedLandmarkType value for that UID.
